author: V.E. Schwab

commentary.text: I read this on a recommendation from my brother in law after complaining about Addie LaRue. He said Vicious is way better. I had heard that elsewhere too, that Addie LaRue was actually her worst book and nothing like any of her other books. I suppose it was a little different, but it felt so hollow. The characters kept commenting about how the undead people were soooo evil, but the only way they ever backed that up was by saying things like "Look at those dead eyes." "Your eyes look dead." "I can just see in your eyes that you're not right." Like, okay? How about giving me an example of something they have done that's evil? Or even enlightening us to a thought process they have that demonstrates their evilness? No, instead the author just tells us the people are evil and we should hate them.

synopsis:
Victor and Eli begin their journey as university roommates—smart, proud, and isolated individuals who quickly spot a mutual drive and intellect. During their final year, their joint academic focus on adrenaline, near-death events, and anomalous phenomena leads them to a fascinating hypothesis: given precise circumstances, individuals might unlock incredible, superhuman gifts. However, when they transition from theoretical study to physical trials, the situation turns disastrous.

A decade later, Victor escapes from incarceration, intent on tracking down his former companion turned adversary, supported by a quiet young girl possessing a remarkable power of her own. At the same time, Eli embarks on a crusade to hunt down and eliminate all other extraordinary individuals he encounters, accompanied by a mysterious woman possessing ironclad determination. Wielding immense, dangerous abilities and fueled by past grievances and animosity, the two former friends are on a direct collision course for retribution—raising the ultimate question of who will survive.
title: Vicious
